question: Does supervised completion improve known density on held-out objects and masks, and does that benefit survive acquired-only SART refinement?
density_scale: fixed synthetic model intensity per assumed micrometre; no case normalization or worm physical-unit claim
split_rule: family=index mod4; independent objects and seeds in each split; shared generator classes, not exclusive anatomical families

noise.generation: full sparse-grid noise before mask; identical observations for all arms
noise.sampling: V3 point-grid geometry; synthetic generation directly on sparse grid, not original100x310 noise field

training_masks: exact V3 B inventory; counts13/15/17/20 balanced

training.loss: per-sample missing-ray MSE, then batch mean
training.selection_rule: mean per-object missing-ray L2 equally over fixed masks; first checkpoint wins ties

metrics.density: relativeL2 over full common grid; RMSE; foregroundL2
metrics.boundaries: symmetric mean nearest-boundary distance in micrometres; fixed foreground threshold0.004 model units
metrics.interior: signed bias and MAE in one-pixel-eroded true foreground; no target-based inference or postprocessing
metrics.projection: raw missing-rayL2 separate from reconstructed withheldL2 and acquiredL2/RMSE
metrics.aggregation: masks within independent object, then objects equally; narrow90 primary; separately by family, span and orientation

gate.scope: all primary90 masks; familiar and new orientations also reported

conditional_refinement.initialization: FBP clamped nonnegative inside identical support for both filled arms
conditional_refinement.schedule: same five measured-only SART sweeps for all arms; no pseudo-rays in likelihood
conditional_refinement.decision: report paired density/projection changes without tuning

stopping: No automatic second seed, objective change or parameter sweep. Failure and partial runs retained. Reserved worm files never accessed.

plots.scales: common per-panel intensity/error ranges; physical coordinates
